description:
Could You Travel Through a Wormhole?

Episode 71 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌀
Wormholes: tunnels through space-time allowed by Einstein's equations, first described by Einstein and Rosen in 1935. In 1988 Kip Thorne showed what it would take to keep one open: strange 'exotic matter'. None has ever been found.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 72: Next stop, Sagittarius A*. The giant black hole at the center of our galaxy.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Could you take a shortcut across the universe, through a wormhole?
Imagine space as a sheet of paper. To get from one side to the other, you travel across the page.
segments.headline: Space as a sheet

segments.text: But fold the paper and poke a hole through it, and the two sides touch. That shortcut is a wormhole.
segments.headline: Fold it, poke a hole

segments.text: In nineteen thirty-five, Einstein and Nathan Rosen found that his equations allow these tunnels. They called them bridges.
The catch? Those tunnels would pinch shut instantly. Not even light could make it through.
segments.headline: They snap shut

segments.text: In nineteen eighty-eight, physicist Kip Thorne worked out what it would take to hold one open.
segments.headline: Holding one open

segments.text: You'd need exotic matter, something with negative energy that pushes space apart. No one knows if enough of it can exist.
segments.headline: Exotic matter needed

segments.text: Some scientists think a wormhole could even work as a time machine. Others think nature forbids it.
segments.headline: A time machine?

segments.text: So far, there is zero evidence that wormholes exist. But physics hasn't ruled them out.
Tomorrow, a real monster: the giant black hole at the center of our own galaxy. Next stop: Sagittarius A star. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
